path: ServerScriptService/TutorialService.luau
purpose: Feature: First-60-seconds tutorial: a TutorialGuide client script shows a bouncing 3D arrow (a neon arrow part floating above the target plus a Beam from the player to it) and a short instruction banner that walks a new player through: 1) 'Walk to a CLAIM gate to claim your plot' (points at the nearest free claim gate), 2) 'Watch your dropper make cash' (points at the collector, waits for the first cash-in), 3) 'Step on the glowing pad to buy your first upgrade' (points at the cheapest buy pad), 4) 'Open the SHOP for more' (highlights the SHOP button). Each step advances on the real event; the server fires a TutorialStep remote when the player claims, cashes in and buys. The guide hides itself after the last step or after 60 seconds, whichever is first, and is skipped for a player who has rebirthed or owns 3+ upgrades. Bump counter tutorial_steps. -- Server owner of tutorial state. It creates the RemoteEvent 'TutorialStep' in ReplicatedStorage in one place at require time. API: TutorialService.start() connects Players.PlayerAdded and loops over Players:GetPlayers() once; TutorialService.notify(player, eventName) is called by the existing services. Per-player state records which of 'claimed','cashed','bought' have already fired, so each fires at most once and only in order. On join, start() decides whether to skip: the player has rebirthed or already owns 3+ upgrades. Read how RebirthService and UpgradeService store rebirth count and owned upgrades (leaderstat, attribute or table) and use exactly that. If the player qualifies it fires TutorialStep(player,'skip') and marks them done. Otherwise it fires TutorialStep(player,'start'). notify() fires TutorialStep:FireClient(player, eventName) for a valid next event and bumps ForgeTelemetry.count('tutorial_steps',1) in this one place only. Events after the 60s window or after skip are ignored. Clears state on PlayerRemoving. Uses ForgeTelemetry and TutorialConfig. Bump ForgeTelemetry counters: tutorial_steps.
depends: ReplicatedStorage/TutorialConfig.luau, ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau

```luau
-- Pure shared tunables for the first-60-seconds tutorial.
-- No side effects: this ModuleScript only returns a table.

local TutorialConfig = {
	TOTAL_SECONDS = 60,
	SKIP_UPGRADES = 3,

	REMOTE_NAME = "TutorialStep",

	EVENTS = {
		START = "start",
		CLAIMED = "claimed",
		CASHED = "cashed",
		BOUGHT = "bought",
		SKIP = "skip",

	-- Banner text per step (index = step number).

		"Watch your dropper make cash",
		"Step on the glowing pad to buy your first upgrade",
		"Open the SHOP for more",
	},

	-- Which server event advances away from each step.
	-- step 1 -> advances on 'claimed', step 2 -> 'cashed', step 3 -> 'bought', step 4 -> ends when the shop opens.
	ADVANCE_ON = {

		"cashed",
		"bought",
		"shop",

-- Convenience lookups.
```

### ReplicatedStorage/ForgeTelemetry.luau
```luau
--!strict
-- ForgeTelemetry: tiny counter API for generated games. ForgeProbe reports these counters.
--
--   local ForgeTelemetry = require(game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage").ForgeTelemetry)
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("coins_collected")      -- +1
--   ForgeTelemetry.count("damage_dealt", 25)     -- +25
--   ForgeTelemetry.get()                          -- { coins_collected = 1, damage_dealt = 25 }
--
-- Counters live as number attributes on ServerStorage.ForgeCounters (a Folder), so every VM in the
-- server (game scripts, ForgeProbe, execute_luau) sees the same values. Server only: on the client
-- count() is a no-op and get() returns {}.

local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local FOLDER_NAME = "ForgeCounters"

local ForgeTelemetry = {}

local function folder(): Instance?
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return nil
	end
	local ServerStorage = game:GetService("ServerStorage")
	local f = ServerStorage:FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		f = Instance.new("Folder")
		f.Name = FOLDER_NAME
		f.Parent = ServerStorage
	end
	return f
end

-- Attribute names: letters, digits and underscores, max 100 chars, may not start with "RBX".
local function key(name: string): string
	local k = string.gsub(tostring(name), "[^%w_]", "_")
	if k == "" then
		k = "_"
	end
	if string.sub(k, 1, 3) == "RBX" then
		k = "_" .. k
	end
	return string.sub(k, 1, 100)
end

function ForgeTelemetry.count(name: string, n: number?)
	local f = folder()
	if not f then
		return
	end
	local ok = pcall(function()
		local k = key(name)
		local cur = f:GetAttribute(k)
		local add = tonumber(n) or 1
		f:SetAttribute(k, (if type(cur) == "number" then cur else 0) + add)
	end)
	if not ok then
		-- telemetry must never break the game
		return
	end
end

function ForgeTelemetry.get(): { [string]: number }
	local out: { [string]: number } = {}
	if not RunService:IsServer() then
		return out
	end
	local f = game:GetService("ServerStorage"):FindFirstChild(FOLDER_NAME)
	if not f then
		return out
	end
	for k, v in f:GetAttributes() do
		if type(v) == "number" then
			out[k] = v
		end
	end
	return out
end

return ForgeTelemetry

```

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.

## Luau and Roblox APIs
- The base place is empty: build the map from code (Instance.new Parts, Anchored = true, parented to Workspace).
- Get services with game:GetService("Players") etc.; use task.wait / task.spawn / task.delay, never wait / spawn / delay.
- Players.PlayerAdded can fire before your script connects in a playtest: also loop over Players:GetPlayers() once at startup.
- Wait for characters with player.CharacterAdded (and player.Character if already present); use WaitForChild with a timeout across the client/server boundary.
- ModuleScripts must return exactly one value (usually a table); require them by path, e.g. require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("Config")).
- Create RemoteEvents on the server in one place; clients only WaitForChild them and handle nil after the timeout.
- Bump counters for key gameplay events with require(ReplicatedStorage.ForgeTelemetry).count("name", 1) (server only) so playtests can verify the core loop. Include counters for purchases and other branches that need verification.
- Count each telemetry counter in exactly one place (the module that owns the event). Duplicate count calls push once-only counters past their expected value.
- Touched fires many times per touch: debounce per player (a per-player cooldown or a one-time purchased flag) and check and deduct cost in the same step to prevent double-buys or double-spends.
- Define the data shape that a builder module returns (field names such as origin, gate, spawn) once, and have consumers use those exact fields. Do not add `a or b` fallbacks for guessed names.

## Fixing and debugging
- A "sync" StudioError about not being able to serve a path is an infrastructure or environment failure, not a code bug. Do not change game code in response. Retry the step.
- If the critic says a code path was never exercised in the playtest, fix the pacing or setup so the path actually runs (e.g. cheaper first purchase) instead of only adding more code.
- When the spec changes the flow (e.g. from auto-assign to claim), rewrite the entry script (Game.server) to require and wire the new modules, and delete the old flow's logic (slots, teleport on join). Updating only the new modules leaves the old behaviour running.
- After a redesign, check that every module is required by the entry script and that its init function is called. Unwired modules never run, and their counters never fire.

```luau
--!strict
-- TutorialService: server owner of first-60-seconds tutorial state.
-- Creates the 'TutorialStep' RemoteEvent at require time; other services call notify().

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local TutorialConfig = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("TutorialConfig"))
local ForgeTelemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry"))

local EVENTS = TutorialConfig.EVENTS

-- One place that creates the remote.
local remote: RemoteEvent
do
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(TutorialConfig.REMOTE_NAME)
	if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		remote = existing
	else
		remote = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
		remote.Name = TutorialConfig.REMOTE_NAME
		remote.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	end
end

type State = {
	fired: { [string]: boolean },
	done: boolean,
	startedAt: number,
}

local states: { [Player]: State } = {}

-- Ordered events the server drives; each fires at most once and only in order.
local ORDER = { EVENTS.CLAIMED, EVENTS.CASHED, EVENTS.BOUGHT }

local TutorialService = {}

local function numberFrom(inst: Instance?): number
	if inst and (inst:IsA("IntValue") or inst:IsA("NumberValue")) then
		return (inst :: IntValue).Value
	end
	return 0
end

-- Rebirths are stored in the 'Rebirths' leaderstat; owned upgrades are tracked
-- on the player as the 'UpgradesOwned' attribute (0 if nothing is recorded yet).
local function hasRebirthed(player: Player): boolean
	local stats = player:FindFirstChild("leaderstats")
	if stats and numberFrom(stats:FindFirstChild("Rebirths")) > 0 then
		return true
	end
	local attr = player:GetAttribute("Rebirths")
	return type(attr) == "number" and attr > 0
end

local function ownedUpgrades(player: Player): number
	local attr = player:GetAttribute("UpgradesOwned")
	if type(attr) == "number" then
		return attr
	end
	return 0
end

local function isActive(player: Player, state: State?): boolean
	if not state or state.done then
		return false
	end
	if os.clock() - state.startedAt > TutorialConfig.TOTAL_SECONDS then
		state.done = true
		return false
	end
	return player.Parent == Players
end

function TutorialService.notify(player: Player, eventName: string)
	local state = states[player]
	if not state or not isActive(player, state) then
		return
	end
	local nextEvent: string? = nil
	for _, name in ORDER do
		if not state.fired[name] then
			nextEvent = name
			break
		end
	end
	if nextEvent == nil or eventName ~= nextEvent then
		return
	end
	state.fired[eventName] = true
	if eventName == EVENTS.BOUGHT then
		-- last server-driven step; client handles the SHOP step locally
		state.fired[EVENTS.BOUGHT] = true
	end
	ForgeTelemetry.count("tutorial_steps", 1)
	remote:FireClient(player, eventName)
end

local function setup(player: Player)
	if states[player] then
		return
	end
	local state: State = { fired = {}, done = false, startedAt = os.clock() }
	states[player] = state

	task.spawn(function()
		-- leaderstats may not exist yet; wait briefly, then give the client time to load.
		player:WaitForChild("leaderstats", 5)
		task.wait(1.5)
		if states[player] ~= state or player.Parent ~= Players then
			return
		end
		if hasRebirthed(player) or ownedUpgrades(player) >= TutorialConfig.SKIP_UPGRADES then
			state.done = true
			remote:FireClient(player, EVENTS.SKIP)
			return
		end
		remote:FireClient(player, EVENTS.START)
	end)

	task.delay(TutorialConfig.TOTAL_SECONDS + 2, function()
		if states[player] == state then
			state.done = true
		end
	end)
end

local started = false

function TutorialService.start()
	if started then
		return
	end
	started = true
	Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(setup)
	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player)
		states[player] = nil
	end)
	for _, player in Players:GetPlayers() do
		setup(player)
	end
end

return TutorialService
```
